cards.text: One day Jesus gets into a boat with His disciples, and they set out on the lake. Picture it, friend: open water, good company, nothing on the schedule. Jesus tells them exactly where they're headed.

cards.question: Jesus and His disciples are setting out in the boat. Where does Jesus say they're going?

answers.text: To the other side of the lake
Back to the town of Capernaum

cards.question: As they sail across the lake, Jesus stays awake the whole trip.

cards.text: He falls asleep. Then a windstorm comes down on the lake, the boat starts getting swamped, and they are in GREAT danger.

cards.question: Water is filling the disciples' boat and Jesus is asleep. What do the disciples do?

cards.text: They wake Him: “Master, Master, we are perishing!” No “good morning,” no “sorry to bother You,” they go straight to PERISHING.

cards.question: Woken up in the storm, Jesus gets up and ___ the wind and the raging waters.

cards.text: Jesus rebukes the wind and the raging waters, and they settle down until all is calm. That lake goes flat as cookie dough under a rolling pin.
Then Jesus turns to His disciples, real quiet: “Where is your faith?”

cards.question: Jesus has just calmed the storm and asked the disciples where their faith is. How do the disciples feel?
Frightened and amazed after the storm, the disciples ask one another a question. What do they ask?

cards.text: “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!” Friend, I spent YEARS bossing around the rubber bands in my old junk drawer, and not ONE of them ever listened.
Jesus and the disciples sail on to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee. When Jesus steps ashore, a demon-possessed man from the town comes to meet Him.

cards.question: For a long time this demon-possessed man hasn't worn clothes or lived in a house. Where has he been staying?

cards.text: When the man from the tombs sees Jesus, he cries out and falls down before Him.

cards.question: Lying before Jesus, the man shouts in a loud voice. What does he call Jesus?

answers.text: Son of the Most High God

cards.text: “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!” Hey, I know that name, friend, because the Most High is the One who pulled me out of the dark.

cards.question: Many times the unclean spirit had seized this man, and when people bound him with chains and shackles, the chains held him.

cards.text: He broke the chains, and the demon drove him off into solitary places. I sat in a junk drawer for years and never got out on my own, and this man is snapping CHAINS.
Jesus had already commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Now He asks, “What is your name?”

cards.question: The man answers Jesus with the name “Legion” because many ___ had gone into him.

cards.text: The demons keep begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss. Meanwhile, on the hillside, a large herd of pigs is feeding.

cards.question: With a herd of pigs feeding on the hillside, the demons beg Jesus for something. What do they ask?

answers.text: To let them enter the pigs
To let them go to the tombs
To let them stay in the town

cards.question: Jesus gives the demons permission to enter the herd of pigs.

cards.text: So the demons come out of the man and go into the pigs.

cards.question: Once the demons go into the herd of pigs, what does the herd do?

answers.text: Rushes into the lake and drowns

cards.text: The men tending the pigs saw the whole herd rush down the bank into the lake. They run off and report it all over the town and countryside. Can you imagine that call to the boss? “So… about the pigs.”
So the people go out to see what happened, and they come to Jesus. There's the man the demons left, sitting at Jesus' feet.

cards.question: The man who lived in the tombs is now sitting at Jesus' feet, ___ and in his right mind.
The people find the man clothed and in his right mind at Jesus' feet. How do they react?

cards.text: Meanwhile, the people who saw it all tell how the demon-possessed man was healed. That's the kind of story that gets around faster than a group chat.

cards.question: Great fear takes hold of all the people of the region of the Gerasenes. What do they ask Jesus to do?

cards.text: So Jesus gets back in the boat to head back, and the man the demons left begs to go with Him. I get it, friend: when Somebody pulls you out of the dark, you don't want to let Him out of your sight.

cards.question: Jesus lets the man the demons left come with Him in the boat.
Jesus sends the man away with a job to do. What is it?

answers.text: Go home and tell what God has done
Wait at the shore for His return
Go and show himself to the priest

cards.text: Jesus tells him, “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” So the man goes and proclaims all over the town how much Jesus had done for him, and friend, from the tombs to the town square, THAT is a comeback.

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card, but it runs three sentences: the two-sentence quote 'Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!' plus the rubber band joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer moment: Papa Dorin spending years bossing around the rubber bands. The backstory only has rubber band stretching contests. It also says he went quiet in the drawer at first. Jokes may invent small moments around his bakery, not new details about the drawer.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'follows' doesn't fit the sentence. 'Jesus gets up and follows the wind and the raging waters' reads as silly next to 'rebukes' and 'blesses', so the answers don't share the same kind and tone.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates every stop. Stop 1 has 4 multiple choice, 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. Stop 2 has 4, 2 and 1. Stop 3 has 3, 1 and 1.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card opens with the man's first-person quote 'What do You want with me… I beg You not to torture me!' and never says who is speaking. Who it is only appears on the previous choice card, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: This story card runs three sentences: the two-sentence quote from Luke 8:28 plus Papa Dorin's line about the Most High.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke treats the man's chain-breaking as an impressive escape ('this man is snapping CHAINS') and compares it favorably to Papa Dorin never getting out of the drawer 'on my own'. In the text, the demon seized him and drove him into solitary places (Luke 8:29). That is his suffering, not a feat. The joke doesn't look at his situation with respect, and it gives him agency that the text puts on the demon.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card, but it runs three sentences plus the made-up quote: the herders saw it, they report it, and the call-to-the-boss joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites Luke 8:38-39, but its right answer ('Go home and tell what God has done') comes only from Jesus' words in Luke 8:39. Verse 38 holds the man's request and the sending away, which card 8 already asked.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.
